evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError is the single error type, used by Project, User and Task constructors and by Task.markDone
src/domain/task-status.ts: taskStatuses, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus are defined only here; task.ts and repositories.ts import TaskStatus instead of redefining it
src/domain/task.ts: Task.markDone holds the 'already done' rule and builds a new Task, so the constructor checks run again
src/domain/repositories.ts: ProjectRepository, UserRepository and TaskRepository are written in terms of the domain entities; TaskFilter.status uses TaskStatus
src/domain/project.ts and src/domain/user.ts: each constructor checks its own required fields; these are separate per-entity checks, not one shared invariant duplicated
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain files all serve one concern: the task-management domain model. That covers the entities (Project, User, Task), a value type (TaskStatus), the domain error type (DomainError) and the repository ports (ProjectRepository, UserRepository, TaskRepository, TaskFilter). The abstractions are used the same way throughout. Every entity reports validation failures with DomainError. Task and TaskFilter type status as TaskStatus, and the repository interfaces work with the domain entity types rather than raw data. Each invariant lives in one place. The list of allowed status values and the isTaskStatus guard are only in task-status.ts. The rule that a task can't be marked done twice is only in Task.markDone. Due-date validation is only in the Task constructor. Project and User have similar "id and name are required" checks, but each one belongs to its own entity's constructor, so this is not one shared rule that has been copied. No file goes around the module's own abstractions.
